summary: Fire tower built 1934 near Olanta, SC; the name Lee-Matthews appears only in a 1934 newspaper item, so its link to the garden tower is inferred from date and place. Moved in 2004 to Moore Farms Botanical Garden near Lake City, where it stands as a garden landmark.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a bright red top
facts.status_note: The original Olanta site has no tower on recent imagery, per an OpenStreetMap note. The tower stands at Moore Farms Botanical Garden, Lake City.

access.note: The garden is not open to the public daily. Visitors can see the property through tours, events, or camps and classes; tours are booked at least two weeks ahead. The pages read do not say whether the tower may be climbed.

events.note: Under construction in April 1934 near Olanta, on ten acres given by DeLeon Lee and Alex Matthews
Bought at a silent auction in Olanta (garden) or purchased from the SC Forestry Commission (register); moved to Moore Farms Botanical Garden
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as Moore Farms Botanical Garden Lookout

corrections.why: The tower was moved in 2004 from Olanta to Moore Farms Botanical Garden, where it stands. The brief's status did not record the move.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's Built field gives 2004, the year of the move, while its description gives 1934 as the original build year at Olanta. The story uses 1934 for the build and 2004 for the move.
The register says the tower was purchased from the Forestry Commission; the garden says it was bought at a silent auction in Olanta. Both may describe the same sale; neither source names the process.

notes_for_editor: The link between the Lee-Matthews name and the Moore Farms tower is inferred, not stated by any one source. The eastern lookouts page names a 1934 Olanta tower Lee-Matthews; only the register gives the 1934 build year at Olanta; the garden page mentions neither 1934 nor Lee-Matthews. The story states the link as an inference from the shared 1934 date and Olanta site. An editor should confirm this before publication. Height: the garden page gives both 'Standing more than 100 feet tall' and a '100-foot steel tower'; height_m 30.5 follows the 100-foot figure. The register's elevation (91 ft) is the garden site, not the tower. Access: the visit page offers tours, events, and camps or classes, with tours booked at least two weeks ahead; climbing is not addressed in the pages read. The NHLR entry credits a photo by Ethan Kauffman, but no image URL was found, so no photo is recorded. The OSM fixme on the original point is a community note, not a survey.
